answer: Each new key must tend a vine: an append-only tendril of work leaves, each countersigned by a distinct established peer whose own tendril shares no root with it. The key then emits a uniqueness signal — a beacon whose phase is bound to the current tip hash. When the settlement tide recedes, the protocol clusters keys whose beacons stay phase-locked or whose tendrils braid through the same first attesters; that cohort is slashed in proportion to how many identities collapsed together, and those tips may not graft new leaves for two epochs.
